analysis_refs.heading: 2. Twenty categories and how to find candidates for each
analysis_refs.text: | C15 Historical documents, manuscripts and archives | National/archive association directories, Library of Congress, Europeana and regional aggregators | National/state archives, university special collections and regional manuscript initiatives | Collection search/export with digitized-item links; IIIF may describe/view an item but does not itself prove catalog search |

analysis_refs.heading: 2. Twenty categories and how to find candidates for each
analysis_refs.text: | C16 Art, museum and cultural-heritage resources | Europeana institution providers, museum open-access programs and cultural institution directories | National/state museums, cultural academies and university museums | Collection APIs/exports; item identity, captions, provenance and image/object rights; metadata-only objects excluded from usable-access totals |

analysis_refs.heading: 3. Discovery engines to use before broad web searching
analysis_refs.text: | [Europeana APIs](https://www.europeana.eu/en/apis) | Search and record interfaces with institutional attribution for cultural material | Universal image/full-object rights; a free API key still needs registration and policy review |

analysis_refs.heading: C16 — Museums, art and cultural heritage
analysis_refs.text:
**Where to start.** [Europeana's API overview](https://www.europeana.eu/en/apis)
describes search, record and harvesting routes with contributing institutions.
Use provider attribution to discover museums across countries, then check the
institution's own open-collection policy. In India,
[Museums of India's digitization initiative](https://museumsofindia.gov.in/repository/page/digitization_initiative)
links participating museums, with JATAN as the collection-management context.
This is a useful network of leads; it does not establish a public integration API.
For the US investigate museum open-access programs and official collection
developer pages, including Smithsonian as a lead requiring renewed documentation.

analysis_refs.heading: C17 — Newspapers, magazines and public-interest articles
analysis_refs.text:
**Where to start.** Separate historic newspaper repositories from current
publishers. The [Library of Congress Chronicling America API page](https://www.loc.gov/apis/additional-apis/chronicling-america-api/)
states that the collection moved exclusively to the loc.gov API beginning in
2025; do not reuse old `chroniclingamerica.loc.gov` integration recipes.
Europeana and national libraries provide additional historical leads. For current
US/local journalism, [INN's Find Your News directory](https://findyournews.org/)
leads to publishers by place and topic. India's
[Press Registrar title directory](https://prgi.gov.in/en/test/registred-titles)
supports discovery by publication place, state and language. Registration proves
neither free article access nor permission to reuse metadata.

analysis_refs.heading: Evidence limits and research handoff
analysis_refs.text:
This pass reviewed official documentation and directory pages on 2026-11-05.
NARA, Archives Portal Europe, National Archives of India, Museums of India,
Bharatavani, Europeana, PRGI, INN/Find Your News, loc.gov, NPTEL, Internet Archive,
Commons and WordPress pages were retrievable. OLAC FAQ and LINCS direct opens
returned 403 despite official search-index descriptions; treat those details as
leads pending direct recheck. Smithsonian `openaccess/devtools` and
`openaccess/faq` opens returned 404 despite indexed results; locate their current
official documentation before qualification. These observations do not establish
service-wide failure or full-item availability.

analysis_refs.heading: Credentials and implementation inputs
analysis_refs.text:
1. Verify **`OPENALEX_API_KEY`** in the backend. The replacement environment reports the variable configured; no authenticated OpenAlex request was made during this repository transfer. At the research date the free account included $1/day of API usage, roughly 1,000 ordinary search requests before caching. Disable paid overages unless deliberately budgeted.
2. Choose a real **application contact email** for request identification and, if enabled, Unpaywall's required `email` parameter. No email was invented, registered, or sent during this work.
3. Optional later: Semantic Scholar, BHL and Europeana keys; CORE upgrade/eligibility confirmation. Standard Ebooks feed access and children's/OER catalog feeds need provider-specific arrangements.

analysis_refs.heading: Blocked connector access report
analysis_refs.text: The strongest immediate self-service options are Data.gov, Census, Europeana and DPLA. India OGD remains conditional on service recovery and a documented resource API. NARA accepts emailed requests; Semantic Scholar requires review of the intended use; Unpaywall needs a contact email for DOI lookup, not a new keyword-search API.
